transcript.text: kettle keeps tripin the electrics, whole kitchen goes off. not evry time maybe 1 in 4. is it the kettle or the fusebox?? need my tea lol

Sounds more likely to be the kettle, especially if it only happens when the kettle is used and it’s intermittent. A failing kettle element, water getting into the base, or a damaged lead can trip an RCD/RCBO even before it fails completely.

For now:
• Stop using that kettle and unplug it. Don’t keep resetting the switch and trying again.
• Check the plug, cable and base for damage, dampness, burning smell, scorch marks or a loose connection. Don’t open it.
• If possible, use a different kettle in that socket/circuit. If the replacement works repeatedly without tripping, bin/replace the old kettle.
• Don’t use extension leads or adapters as a workaround.

At the consumer unit/fusebox:
• If the switch labelled RCD, RCBO, or one protecting several circuits trips, that often points to an appliance leaking current to earth — a kettle is a common culprit.
• If only the kitchen sockets breaker trips, it could still be the kettle, but also an overloaded or faulty kitchen circuit/socket.

Call an electrician if:
• it trips with the kettle unplugged,
• other appliances cause it too,
• the breaker/RCD will not stay on,
• there’s heat, buzzing, burning smell, sparks, or visible damage.

For tea: use a pan on the hob only if the hob is unaffected and safe to use; otherwise, wait for a replacement kettle/electrician.

ok i had a look, base has a bit of brown crusty stuff on the contacts. i did overfill it last week and water went all over the base, prob not related lol. it did make a little crackle once and i got a tiny tingle touching it and the tap but thought it was static. no burny smell tho

That is not static to assume away. A tingle from the kettle/tap plus crackling and tripping means a possible electric-shock fault, very likely made worse by water getting into the base.

Stop using it now. Do not touch the kettle, its base, plug, or the tap while it’s plugged in.

If you can do so without touching anything damp/metal:
1. Dry your hands, stand on a dry floor, and switch off the kitchen sockets circuit at the consumer unit/fusebox (or the main switch if you can’t identify it).
2. Once power is off, unplug the kettle. Leave it unplugged and replace it — don’t try to clean the contacts, dry it out, or test it again.

Because you felt a tingle, I’d avoid using other kitchen sockets until you’ve checked things:
• If the circuit stays on with the kettle removed and other appliances work normally, the kettle is almost certainly the problem.
• If it still trips, or you get any tingles from taps/appliances, leave the circuit off and get an electrician urgently. That can indicate an appliance fault, socket fault, or earthing issue.

If anyone gets a proper shock, has chest pain, burns, weakness, or feels unwell, seek urgent medical help. If there is smoke, sparks, heat, or burning, turn power off if safe and call emergency services.

No tea from that kettle, unfortunately. Use the hob only if it is separate, working normally, and there are no electrical symptoms around it.
